name: Mandatory Annual Compliance Training
description: A comprehensive annual training program for staff covering a wide range of regulatory and operational requirements. It encompasses AML, KYC, GDPR, fraud prevention, and reporting obligations to ensure customer protection and regulatory adherence.
context: Mandatory annual compliance training covering regulatory requirements, customer protection, anti-money laundering (AML), know-your-customer (KYC), GDPR, fraud prevention, and reporting obligations.

name: Module 1: AML & Sanctions Compliance
description: A mandatory annual training module focusing on Anti-Money Laundering and Sanctions compliance. It requires a quiz pass rate of 80% or higher for completion.
context: Assessment: Quiz at end of each module (pass = 80%+)

name: Module 2: Know Your Customer (KYC)
description: A mandatory annual training module covering Know Your Customer (KYC) procedures. Completion is required for all staff and validated via a quiz.
context: Assessment: Quiz at end of each module (pass = 80%+)

name: Module 3: GDPR & Data Protection
description: A mandatory annual training module regarding GDPR and general data protection standards. Staff must achieve 80% or more on the final quiz.
context: Assessment: Quiz at end of each module (pass = 80%+)

name: Module 4: Fraud Prevention
description: A mandatory annual training module dedicated to fraud prevention techniques. Completion is verified by a quiz with a minimum pass mark of 80%.
context: Assessment: Quiz at end of each module (pass = 80%+)

name: Module 5: Reporting Obligations
description: A mandatory annual training module detailing the reporting obligations of bank staff. Requires a quiz score of 80% or higher for certification.
context: Assessment: Quiz at end of each module (pass = 80%+)

name: Module 6: Consequences of Non-Compliance
description: A mandatory annual training module explaining the repercussions of failing to comply with bank and regulatory standards. Completion is marked by a quiz pass of 80% or more.
context: Assessment: Quiz at end of each module (pass = 80%+)

name: Mandatory Annual Training Completion
description: An obligation for all staff to complete the six mandatory training modules annually or immediately following regulatory changes.
context: Frequency: Annual (or immediately upon change in regulations)

name: Module 1 — AML & Sanctions Compliance
description: A foundational training unit covering the principles of Anti-Money Laundering (AML) and sanctions compliance. It defines money laundering and outlines the legal and regulatory consequences of non-compliance for FirstUK Bank.
context: Money laundering is the process of converting illegally obtained money into legitimate-looking funds.

name: Identification and Reporting of Suspicious Activity
description: The requirement for staff to be able to recognize indicators of money laundering and follow the correct procedures to report such activity.
context: Your role: Identify and report suspicious activity

name: Compliance with Money Laundering Regulations 2017
description: The legal obligation for FirstUK Bank and its staff to adhere to the UK Money Laundering Regulations 2017 to prevent the conversion of illegal funds.
context: FirstUK Bank must comply with UK law (Money Laundering Regulations 2017)

name: The AML Process
description: A training section outlining the sequential workflow for handling suspicious activity, from initial detection through to potential law enforcement action.

name: Suspicious Activity Detected
description: The primary trigger event in the AML workflow where staff identify activity that warrants further scrutiny.

name: Report to Compliance Team
description: The mandatory internal requirement to escalate detected suspicious activity to the bank's Compliance Team for further review.

name: Report to FCA (if necessary)
description: The regulatory obligation to report findings to the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) following the completion of an internal investigation.

name: Multiple large deposits followed by immediate large withdrawals
description: A high-risk transaction pattern where significant funds are deposited and then quickly removed from the account, often indicative of layering in money laundering.
context: Multiple large deposits followed by immediate large withdrawals

name: Frequent transfers to multiple accounts or jurisdictions
description: A pattern of moving funds across various accounts or international borders frequently, which may be used to obscure the audit trail.

name: Round-number transactions
description: Transactions occurring in exact round sums (e.g., £10k, £20k), which are often atypical for genuine commercial or personal activity.

name: Transfers to high-risk countries
description: The movement of funds to jurisdictions identified as high-risk for money laundering, terrorism financing, or subject to sanctions.

name: Transactions inconsistent with customer profile
description: Financial activity that does not align with the known occupation, income, or expected behavior of the customer.
context: Example: A pensioner suddenly transferring £50,000 to a shell company in Panama

name: Reluctance to provide documentation
description: A high-risk customer behavior where the individual is unwilling or hesitant to provide the necessary identification or supporting documents required for account verification.

name: Vague about purpose of account
description: A high-risk indicator where a customer cannot or will not provide a clear, logical explanation for why they are opening a bank account.

name: Changes story about transaction purpose
description: A high-risk behavioral pattern where a customer provides inconsistent or contradictory explanations regarding the nature or purpose of their financial transactions.

name: Uses third party as proxy
description: A high-risk scenario where a customer utilizes another person to act on their behalf to obscure the true identity of the account holder or the source of funds.

name: Avoids using account normally after opening
description: A high-risk indicator where the account activity does not align with standard customer usage patterns immediately following the account opening process.
context: Avoids using account normally after opening

name: Account opening followed by large deposit and third-party withdrawal
description: A specific high-risk example involving the rapid movement of funds where a new account is used to deposit a significant sum which is then immediately withdrawn by a third party.
context: Customer opens account, deposits £30,000, then has friend withdraw it

name: Money services (remittance) Business Activity
description: Identification of a customer operating in the money services or remittance sector, which is classified as a high-risk business activity.

name: Casinos and Gambling Business Activity
description: Identification of a customer operating in the casinos or gambling sector, classified as a high-risk business activity.

name: Art Dealers and Jewelers Business Activity
description: Identification of a customer operating as an art dealer or jeweler, which is categorized as a high-risk business activity.

name: Cash-intensive Retail Business Activity
description: Identification of a customer operating a retail business that is heavily reliant on cash transactions, classified as high-risk.

name: Used Car Dealerships Business Activity
description: Identification of a customer operating a used car dealership, which is listed as a high-risk business activity.

name: High-value Goods (Watches, Handbags) Business Activity
description: Identification of a customer dealing in high-value goods such as watches and handbags, categorized as a high-risk business activity.

name: Customer Association with OFAC Listed Countries (Geographic Risk)
description: A red flag identified when a customer is associated with countries listed by the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC), indicating high geographic risk.
context: OFAC List: Iran, North Korea, Syria, Crimea, Cuba, Sudan

name: Customer Association with EU Consolidated List Entities (Geographic Risk)
description: A risk indicator triggered by associations with various sanctioned entities as defined by the EU Consolidated List.
context: EU Consolidated List: Various sanctioned entities

name: Customer Association with HMT Sanctioned Entities (Geographic Risk)
description: A red flag involving associations with additional entities sanctioned by Her Majesty's Treasury (HMT) within the UK.

name: Customer Association with High-Corruption Countries (Geographic Risk)
description: A geographic risk indicator where customers are linked to countries identified as having high levels of corruption, specifically Nigeria, Zimbabwe, and Venezuela.

name: Screening Requirements Training
description: A training section detailing the mandatory screening procedures for new customers during the account opening process to ensure compliance with international sanctions and PEP lists.

name: New Customer Screening Process Knowledge
description: Staff must be able to execute the full screening workflow for new customers, including data collection, list checking, and result documentation.
context: Screen against: OFAC, EU Consolidated List, HMT Sanctions, UN Sanctions, PEP Database

name: Mandatory Sanctions and PEP Screening
description: The requirement to screen new customers against specific global sanctions lists and the PEP database before an account is permitted to open.
context: Screen against: OFAC, EU Consolidated List, HMT Sanctions, UN Sanctions, PEP Database
must be clear before account opens

name: Immediate Compliance Escalation for Screening Matches
description: The obligation to immediately notify the Compliance department if a customer match is found during the screening process.
context: If match found: Escalate to Compliance immediately

name: Screening Result Documentation
description: The requirement for staff to formally document the outcome of the screening process for every new customer.

name: Sanctions or PEP List Match
description: A positive match found when screening a customer against OFAC, EU, HMT, UN, or PEP databases, indicating a high-risk individual.
context: If match found: Escalate to Compliance immediately

name: New Customer
description: An individual seeking to open a new account who is subject to the bank's initial screening requirements.

name: New Account
description: A bank account in the process of being opened, which cannot be activated until screening results are clear.
context: must be clear before account opens

name: Sanctions and PEP Screening Process
description: The process of verifying new customers against international sanctions lists (OFAC, EU, HMT, UN) and Politically Exposed Persons (PEP) databases.
context: Screen against: OFAC, EU Consolidated List, HMT Sanctions, UN Sanctions, PEP Database
Review results (must be clear before account opens)

name: New Customer Identity Collection
description: The initial step of the KYC process involving the collection of basic identity markers from a new customer.

name: Monthly Transaction Review Obligation
description: A requirement for staff to conduct monthly reviews of high-value transactions and monitor for unusual activity to ensure ongoing compliance.

name: Monthly Sanctions Screening Obligation
description: A mandatory monthly requirement to screen customers or transactions against the most current sanctions lists.

name: Ongoing Customer Risk Assessment Obligation
description: The requirement to periodically assess the risk level of existing customers as part of ongoing monitoring.

name: Transaction Halt Obligation on Sanctions Match
description: A strict requirement to stop the processing of any transaction if a sanctions match is identified.

name: Compliance Escalation Duty
description: The obligation to report a sanctions match or suspicious finding to the Compliance department immediately.

name: Anti-Tipping Off Prohibition
description: A legal prohibition against informing a customer that they are under investigation or that a match has been found, as this constitutes illegal tipping-off.
context: Do NOT inform customer (tipping-off is illegal)

name: High Value Transaction (>£5,000) Indicator
description: Transactions exceeding £5,000 are identified as a threshold requiring specific monthly review.

name: Unusual Transaction Patterns
description: The identification of transaction behaviors that deviate from the norm and require further investigation.

name: Sanctions List Match
description: A positive match found during the screening of a customer or transaction against updated sanctions lists.

name: OFAC Sanctions List
description: A sanctions list covering US-sanctioned parties, specifically mentioning regions such as Iran, North Korea, and Syria.
context: OFAC | US-sanctioned parties (Iran, North Korea, Syria, etc.)

name: EU Consolidated Sanctions List
description: A sanctions list containing individuals and entities sanctioned by the European Union.
context: EU Consolidated | EU-sanctioned individuals and entities

name: HMT Sanctions List
description: A sanctions list covering parties sanctioned by the UK Home Treasury.

name: UN Sanctions List
description: A sanctions list containing individuals and entities sanctioned by the United Nations.
context: UN Sanctions | UN-sanctioned individuals and entities

name: PEP Database
description: A database used to identify Politically Exposed Persons, who are categorized as high-risk individuals.
context: PEP Database | Politically Exposed Persons (high-risk individuals)

name: Adverse Media Screening
description: A screening process to identify individuals who have appeared in news reports related to financial crime.
context: Adverse Media | Individuals in news for financial crime

name: Escalation of Potential Sanctions Matches
description: Staff are required to escalate potential matches to the Compliance department and must refrain from processing the associated transaction.
context: Escalate to Compliance, do not process

name: Anti-Tipping Off Prohibition
description: A strict legal prohibition against disclosing to a customer that they are being screened against sanctions lists.
context: Do not disclose screening to customer (tipping-off is illegal)

name: Suspicious Activity Reporting Prior to Account Closure
description: Staff must report suspicious activity to the Compliance department before taking the action of closing a customer account.
context: Report suspicious activity to Compliance first

name: Continuous Customer Screening Requirement
description: The obligation to perform screening throughout the entire duration of the customer relationship, rather than only at the point of account opening.

name: Ignoring Potential Sanctions Match
description: A critical operational failure where a staff member ignores a potential sanctions match and proceeds with a transaction.
context: Ignoring a potential match and processing transaction anyway

name: Tipping Off Customer Regarding Sanctions Screening
description: A behavioral red flag where staff explicitly inform a customer that they are being checked against sanctions lists.
context: Telling customer "We're checking if you're on a sanctions list"

name: Premature Account Closure Without Investigation
description: The act of closing an account without first conducting a proper investigation or reporting the suspicion to Compliance.

name: One-Time Only Screening at Onboarding
description: A failure in the screening process where checks are only performed during account opening and neglected thereafter.

name: Module 2: Know Your Customer (KYC)
description: A training module focused on the fundamental requirements of the Know Your Customer (KYC) process, detailing the core rules banks must follow to verify customer identities and assess risk.
context: KYC rules require banks to: 1. Collect customer identity information 2. Verify customer identity 3. Understand customer's business/source of funds 4. Assess customer's risk level

name: Collect customer identity information
description: The requirement for staff to be able to gather the necessary identity information from a customer as part of the KYC process.

name: Verify customer identity
description: The requirement for staff to validate the authenticity of the identity information collected from the customer.

name: Understand customer's business/source of funds
description: The requirement for staff to determine and document the nature of the customer's business and the origin of their wealth/funds.

name: Assess customer's risk level
description: The requirement for staff to evaluate the risk profile of a customer based on the collected and verified information.

name: KYC Identity Collection and Verification Obligation
description: A mandatory compliance requirement for the bank to collect and verify customer identity information, understand fund sources, and assess risk levels.
context: KYC rules require banks to: 1. Collect customer identity information 2. Verify customer identity 3. Understand customer's business/source of funds 4. Assess customer's risk level

name: KYC Process
description: The overarching Know Your Customer process used to ensure the bank has verified the identity and risk profile of its clients.
context: KYC rules require banks to: 1. Collect customer identity information 2. Verify customer identity

name: Bank Customer
description: The individual or entity whose identity must be collected, verified, and risk-assessed under KYC rules.

name: Primary Identity Document Verification Requirement
description: Staff must collect and verify a valid primary identity document from the customer. The document must be an original and cannot be a photocopy or an expired document.

name: Passport Verification Procedure
description: When using a UK Passport for identity verification, staff must ensure the original is valid, copy both sides, and inspect the document for signs of tampering.

name: Driving License Verification Procedure
description: When using a UK Driving License for identity verification, staff must ensure the original is valid, copy both sides, and verify that the photo matches the customer.

name: Expired Identity Documentation (KYC Red Flag)
description: The presentation of expired identity documents is flagged as unacceptable for the KYC process.

name: Submission of Photocopies Only (KYC Red Flag)
description: The attempt to provide photocopies of identity documents without the original is flagged as unacceptable.

name: Non-UK Identity Documentation (KYC Red Flag)
description: The presentation of identity documents from countries other than the UK is flagged as unacceptable under this specific requirement.

name: Customer
description: The individual undergoing the identity verification process whose documents are being checked.

name: Primary Identity Document Verification Process
description: The process of collecting and validating primary identity documents, specifically UK Passports or UK Driving Licenses, to verify a customer's identity.

name: Proof of Address Verification
description: The process of verifying a customer's residential address using approved documentation. The process specifies acceptable document types and strict validity criteria.
context: Must show customer name and address

name: Utility Bill Validity Requirement
description: Requirement that utility bills used for address verification must be dated within a three-month window and contain specific customer details.
context: Must show customer name and address

name: Council Tax Letter Validity Requirement
description: Requirement that Council Tax letters used for address verification must be from the current year and contain specific customer details.
context: Must show customer name and address

name: Bank Statement Validity Requirement
description: Requirement that bank statements used for address verification must be dated within a three-month window and contain specific customer details.
context: Must show customer name and address

name: Address Document Filing Obligation
description: The mandatory action to create a copy of the accepted proof of address document and file it in the customer records.

name: Unacceptable Address Documentation (KYC Red Flag)
description: Identification of documents that are explicitly prohibited for use as proof of address, including expired documents and specific tax or utility types.

name: Customer
description: The individual whose identity and address are being verified through the submission of supporting documentation.
context: Must show customer name and address

name: New Customer
description: An individual applying for a new account who must undergo a comprehensive verification process before the account can be opened.

name: New Customer Identity Verification Obligation
description: A mandatory set of verification steps that must be completed for every new customer, including ID authenticity, photo matching, and document validity.

name: Proof of Address Verification Obligation
description: The requirement to obtain and verify a proof of address document that is dated within a specific three-month window.
context: Proof of address dated within 3 months

name: Secure Document Filing and Record Completion Obligation
description: The duty to ensure that all verified customer documents are filed securely and that the system record is fully completed.

name: Sanctions Screening Obligation
description: The requirement to check new customers against sanctions lists to ensure there are no matches before proceeding.

name: Verification Failure Escalation Obligation
description: A strict prohibition against opening an account if any verification check fails, with a mandatory requirement to escalate the matter to a manager.
context: If Any Check Fails: Do not open account.

name: New Customer Verification Process
description: The comprehensive KYC checklist used to verify the identity and address of new customers and screen them against sanctions lists.

name: Sanctions List Screening
description: The process of checking a new customer's details against sanctions lists as part of the onboarding verification.

name: New Account
description: An account intended to be opened for a new customer, contingent upon the successful completion of the verification checklist.

name: Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD) Training
description: A training section focused on the Enhanced Due Diligence process for customers identified as higher-risk. It outlines the specific customer categories requiring EDD and the additional verification steps necessary.

name: High-Net-Worth Individual (>£500k) (KYC Red Flag)
description: A risk indicator where a customer is identified as a high-net-worth individual with assets exceeding £500,000, triggering the need for Enhanced Due Diligence.

name: Politically Exposed Person (PEP) (KYC Red Flag)
description: A risk indicator where a customer is identified as a Politically Exposed Person, requiring higher scrutiny and EDD processes.

name: Business in High-Risk Industry (KYC Red Flag)
description: A risk indicator where a business customer operates within an industry classified as high-risk, necessitating enhanced verification.

name: Customer in High-Risk Country (KYC Red Flag)
description: A risk indicator where a customer is located in or associated with a high-risk jurisdiction, triggering EDD requirements.

name: Verify Source of Funds
description: A mandatory requirement to verify the origin of the customer's funds as part of the Enhanced Due Diligence process for high-risk customers.

name: Obtain Business Documents
description: A mandatory requirement to collect and verify official business documentation for high-risk corporate entities.

name: Understand Purpose of Account
description: A mandatory requirement to establish and document the intended nature and purpose of the account for high-risk customers.

name: Ongoing Monitoring
description: A continuous compliance duty to monitor the activity of high-risk accounts to ensure it aligns with the established customer profile.

name: Regular Review
description: A mandatory requirement to perform periodic reviews of high-risk customer files to ensure due diligence remains current.

name: Higher-Risk Customer
description: Customers who meet specific risk criteria (HNW, PEP, high-risk industry/country) and are therefore subject to Enhanced Due Diligence.

name: Enhanced Due Diligence Process
description: The specialized KYC process involving additional verification steps for customers identified as high-risk.

name: Original Identity Document Verification Obligation
description: Staff are strictly prohibited from opening accounts without first inspecting the original identification documents. The required process is to verify the original document before creating a copy.
context: Opening account without seeing original ID

name: Address Proof Recency Requirement
description: Staff must ensure that any document provided as proof of address is current. Documents dated more than three months ago are not acceptable.
context: Accepting address proof dated >3 months ago

name: Documentation-Based Verification Obligation
description: Staff must rely exclusively on formal documentation for verification purposes. Verbal descriptions provided by the customer are insufficient and must not be used as a substitute for documentation.
context: Relying on verbal description instead of documentation

name: Universal KYC Application Obligation
description: Know Your Customer (KYC) procedures must be applied to every single customer without exception. Personal rapport or the perceived nature of the customer does not waive this requirement.
context: KYC applies to EVERY customer, no exceptions

name: KYC Verification Process
description: The overarching process of verifying customer identity and address through original documentation to prevent unauthorized account opening.

name: Bank Customer
description: The individual seeking to open an account or undergo verification, to whom KYC obligations apply regardless of their demeanor.

name: New Bank Account
description: An account in the process of being opened, which triggers the mandatory requirement for original ID verification.
context: Opening account without seeing original ID

name: Module 3 — GDPR & Data Protection
description: A training unit focused on the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), covering the legal framework for the collection, usage, and storage of personal data within the EU and UK.
context: EU/UK data protection law that regulates how companies collect, use, and store personal data.

name: Lawfulness Principle
description: A fundamental data protection requirement ensuring that all processing of personal data is conducted legally and has a valid justification.
context: Data processing must be legal and justified

name: Fairness Principle
description: A requirement to maintain transparency with customers regarding how their data is handled.

name: Purpose Limitation Principle
description: A restriction ensuring that data is only utilized for the specific purposes for which it was originally stated.
context: Only use data for stated purpose

name: Data Minimization Principle
description: A mandate to limit data collection to only the information that is strictly necessary for the intended purpose.

name: Accuracy Principle
description: The obligation to ensure that customer data is kept current and correct.

name: Storage Limitation Principle
description: A requirement to retain data only for the duration necessary to fulfill its purpose.
context: Only keep data as long as necessary

name: Integrity & Confidentiality Principle
description: The duty to protect data using appropriate security measures to ensure integrity and confidentiality.

name: Accountability Principle
description: The obligation to maintain documentation of all data processing activities to demonstrate compliance.
context: Document what you do with data

name: Data Access Request Handling Obligation
description: The mandatory procedure for staff when a customer exercises their right to access their data. It requires acknowledging the request and escalating it to the Data Protection Officer for a response within a specific timeframe.
context: DPO responds within 30 days with all data

name: Customer Requesting Data Access
description: A bank customer who is exercising their legal right to access all personal data held by FirstUK Bank.
context: Customer Request: "I want to see all data you have on me"

name: Right to Erasure Request Handling Obligation
description: The mandatory procedure staff must follow when a customer requests the deletion of their data. This involves a specific workflow of acknowledgement, escalation to the Data Protection Officer, and a legal review before deletion.
context: DPO reviews legal requirements (may need to retain for regulatory reasons)

name: Customer Requesting Data Erasure
description: A bank customer who exercises their right to erasure by requesting the deletion of their personal data.

name: Data Portability Request Handling Obligation
description: The mandatory process for handling customer requests for data portability, requiring staff to acknowledge the request and escalate it to the Data Protection Officer.

name: Customer Requesting Data Portability
description: A bank customer exercising their right to have their personal data provided in a portable format.
context: Customer Request: "Give me my data in a portable format"

name: Marketing Opt-Out Processing Obligation
description: The mandatory set of actions staff must take when a customer exercises their right to object to the use of their data for marketing purposes. This includes acknowledgement, cessation of communications, and system documentation.

name: Customer Requesting Marketing Opt-Out
description: A bank customer who has explicitly requested that the bank cease using their personal data for marketing purposes.
context: Customer Request: "Don't use my data for marketing"

name: Right to Restrict Processing Obligation
description: A mandatory requirement for staff to handle customer requests to restrict data processing during investigations. This involves acknowledging the request and pausing processing activities unless legal requirements dictate otherwise.

name: Customer Requesting Data Restriction
description: A bank customer exercising their right to restrict the processing of their personal data during an investigation period.
context: Customer Request: "Don't process my data while you investigate"

name: Identity Verification Data Collection
description: The requirement to collect specific personal identifiers, including name, date of birth, and address, to satisfy identity verification standards.

name: Account Information Collection for Service Provision
description: The obligation to collect account-related information necessary for the provision of banking services.

name: Transaction History Collection for AML Compliance
description: The mandatory collection of transaction history to ensure the bank meets Anti-Money Laundering (AML) compliance requirements.

name: Payment Details Collection for Transaction Processing
description: The requirement to collect payment details to facilitate the processing of financial transactions.

name: Identity Verification Process
description: The process of verifying a customer's identity using their name, date of birth, and address.

name: AML Compliance Monitoring
description: The use of transaction history data to maintain compliance with Anti-Money Laundering regulations.

name: Contact Preference
description: A dynamic field used to capture the customer's preferred method of communication, specifically choosing between email, phone, or SMS.

name: Marketing Consent
description: A placeholder for recording a customer's separate opt-in agreement to receive marketing communications.

name: Product Preferences
description: A variable used to collect information regarding the customer's product preferences to assist in service improvement.

name: Prohibition on Collection of Sensitive Personal Data Without Consent
description: A strict prohibition against the collection of specific sensitive personal data categories unless explicit consent is obtained or a legal requirement exists. This obligation governs the handling of highly sensitive customer information.

name: GDPR Training
description: A mandatory training module for all staff focusing on the protection of customer data and compliance with General Data Protection Regulation standards.
context: Employee training: All staff trained on GDPR

name: Password Confidentiality Obligation
description: A mandatory security requirement prohibiting staff from sharing their access passwords.

name: Workstation Session Management Obligation
description: A requirement for staff to terminate their active sessions by logging out whenever they leave their desk.

name: Customer Data Privacy Obligation
description: A prohibition against discussing sensitive customer information in public settings.

name: Security Concern Reporting Obligation
description: A duty for employees to immediately report any identified security concerns to the appropriate authority.

name: Physical Document Security Obligation
description: A requirement to ensure that physical documents containing sensitive information are locked away when not actively in use.
context: Lock documents when not in use

name: Bank Customer
description: The individuals whose data is protected by the bank's encryption, access controls, and staff training protocols.

name: Stop Further Access to Data
description: The immediate requirement for staff to halt any ongoing unauthorized access to data upon the discovery of a breach.

name: Immediate Managerial Reporting of Breach
description: The obligation for staff to notify their direct manager immediately after discovering a data breach.

name: DPO Breach Notification
description: The requirement to report a discovered data breach to the Data Protection Officer at dpo@firstuk.bank.

name: Prohibition of Breach Concealment
description: A strict prohibition against attempting to hide or cover up a data breach once it has been discovered.
context: Do NOT attempt to cover it up

name: Regulatory and Customer Notification Timeline
description: The obligation for the DPO to notify the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) and affected customers within a 72-hour window following a breach.
context: DPO will notify FCA and customers within 72 hours

name: Affected Customers
description: Customers whose data has been compromised in a breach and must be notified by the DPO.
context: DPO will notify FCA and customers within 72 hours

name: Data Access Request Forwarding Obligation
description: Staff are required to ensure that any customer data access requests are forwarded to the Data Protection Officer (DPO) within a strict 24-hour timeframe.

name: Customer Data Third-Party Sharing Restriction
description: A prohibition against sharing customer data with third parties unless explicit permission has been granted or there is a legal requirement to do so.
context: Sharing customer data with third party without consent
Only share with explicit permission or legal requirement

name: Customer Data Retention and Disposal Obligation
description: Staff must ensure that customer data is not kept longer than necessary and must be deleted or archived once the retention period expires.
context: Keeping customer data longer than necessary

name: Customer Data Confidentiality and Privacy Obligation
description: A requirement to maintain customer privacy by ensuring sensitive conversations regarding customer data are conducted in private areas to prevent overhearing.
context: Discussing customer data in public (overhearing customers)
Have sensitive conversations in private area

name: Ignoring Customer Data Access Request (Data Protection Concern)
description: A failure to act upon a customer's request to access their data, identified as a common mistake in data handling.
context: Mistake 1: Ignoring customer data access request

name: Unauthorized Third-Party Data Sharing (Data Protection Concern)
description: The act of sharing customer data with a third party without obtaining the necessary consent.
context: Mistake 2: Sharing customer data with third party without consent

name: Excessive Data Retention (Data Protection Concern)
description: Maintaining customer data beyond the required or necessary retention period.
context: Mistake 3: Keeping customer data longer than necessary

name: Public Discussion of Customer Data (Data Protection Concern)
description: Discussing sensitive customer information in public areas where it can be overheard by others.
context: Mistake 4: Discussing customer data in public (overhearing customers)

name: Module 4: Fraud Prevention
description: A training unit focused on the definition of fraud and the multi-layered approach FirstUK Bank uses to combat it, including detection, training, education, and response.
context: At FirstUK Bank, we combat fraud through: Detection systems, Staff training, Customer education, Rapid response

name: Unusual transactions (Account Takeover Signal)
description: A behavioral indicator where transaction patterns deviate from the norm, suggesting a fraudster has gained access to a customer's account.

name: Login from new device (Account Takeover Signal)
description: A technical indicator where an account is accessed from an unrecognized device, potentially signaling unauthorized access.

name: Password change (Account Takeover Signal)
description: A security event where a password is changed, which may be a tactic used by fraudsters to lock out the legitimate customer.

name: Account Takeover
description: A type of fraud where a fraudster gains unauthorized access to a customer's bank account.
context: What It Is: Fraudster gains access to customer's account

name: Customer
description: The bank customer whose account is the target of Account Takeover fraud.
context: Fraudster gains access to customer's account

name: Customer Account
description: The financial account subject to unauthorized access and unusual transactions during an account takeover event.
context: Fraudster gains access to customer's account

name: Customer claims 'I didn't authorize this' (Impersonation Indicator)
description: A specific behavioral signal where a customer denies authorizing a transaction, indicating a potential impersonation fraud attempt where a fraudster pretends to be the customer or bank staff.
context: Signs: Customer claims "I didn't authorize this"
Fraudster pretends to be customer or FirstUK staff

name: Identity Verification Obligation
description: A mandatory prevention step requiring staff to verify the identity of the individual to prevent impersonation fraud.

name: Authorization Documentation Requirement
description: A mandatory requirement for staff to document the authorization process as a means of preventing impersonation fraud.

name: Large Transaction (Unauthorized Transaction Indicator)
description: A red flag indicating potential unauthorized account access where a transaction amount is significantly higher than normal customer behavior.

name: Unusual Merchant (Unauthorized Transaction Indicator)
description: A red flag where a transaction occurs at a merchant that does not align with the customer's typical spending patterns.

name: Foreign Location (Unauthorized Transaction Indicator)
description: A red flag identifying transactions originating from a geographic location inconsistent with the customer's known location.

name: Customer Card
description: The payment card used by the customer which may be compromised by a fraudster for unauthorized transactions.
context: Fraudster uses customer's card/account without permission

name: Customer Account
description: The bank account subject to unauthorized access and fraudulent transactions.
context: Fraudster uses customer's card/account without permission

name: Unauthorized Transaction
description: A financial event where a fraudster uses a customer's card or account without their permission.
context: Fraudster uses customer's card/account without permission

name: Insider Fraud Training
description: A training unit focused on the identification and prevention of fraud committed by bank staff members using their internal positions.
context: Staff member uses position to commit fraud

name: Unusual Account Access (Insider Fraud Sign)
description: A red flag where a staff member accesses customer accounts in a manner that is inconsistent with their job role or normal duties.

name: Undocumented Transactions (Insider Fraud Sign)
description: The occurrence of financial transactions that lack the required supporting documentation or audit trail, indicating potential staff misconduct.

name: Authority Abuse (Insider Fraud Sign)
description: A behavioral pattern where a staff member leverages their level of authority to bypass controls or commit fraudulent acts.

name: Whistleblower Reporting Obligation
description: The requirement for staff to utilize whistleblower channels to report suspected insider fraud and misconduct.

name: Customer Seems Coached or Nervous
description: A behavioral indicator during customer interaction where the individual appears to be following a script or exhibiting anxiety, suggesting potential coercion or fraud.

name: Inability to Explain Purpose of Transaction
description: A red flag where a customer is unable to provide a logical or clear explanation for the nature or purpose of a financial transaction.

name: Use of Unusual Channels or Amounts
description: A warning sign triggered when a customer utilizes non-standard banking channels or transaction amounts that are inconsistent with their profile.

name: Third Party Controlling Conversation
description: A high-risk scenario where a third party is present during a customer interaction and dominates or controls the communication.
context: Third party is present and controlling conversation

name: Immediate Cash Request After Deposit
description: A specific transaction pattern where a customer requests a cash withdrawal immediately following a deposit, often indicative of money laundering.

name: Teller Colleague Bypassing Controls
description: An internal red flag where a staff member intentionally avoids or overrides established banking controls.

name: Teller Colleague Working Unusual Hours Alone
description: An internal behavioral indicator where a staff member works outside of standard hours without supervision.

name: Teller Colleague With Unauthorized Access
description: A security red flag where a staff member possesses system or physical access rights beyond their authorized role.

name: Teller Colleague Making Undocumented Exceptions
description: An internal red flag where a staff member grants exceptions to policy or procedure without maintaining the required documentation.

name: Your Role in Fraud Prevention
description: A training section focused on the staff's responsibility in identifying and responding to fraudulent activity within the bank.

name: Recognize Fraud
description: The ability for staff to identify potential fraud by monitoring transactions, questioning anomalies, and trusting professional instincts.
context: Ask questions if something seems off

name: Report Fraud Concerns
description: A mandatory requirement for staff to report any concerns regarding potential fraud to the appropriate channels.

name: Suspicious Transaction Patterns
description: Transactions that exhibit unusual or suspicious characteristics that require staff monitoring and investigation.

name: Prohibition of Confronting Fraudsters
description: A mandatory prohibition preventing staff from directly confronting individuals suspected of committing fraud during the escalation process.

name: Fraud Observation Documentation Requirement
description: A requirement for staff to record and document their observations when fraud is suspected as part of the escalation workflow.

name: Managerial Fraud Reporting Obligation
description: The duty for staff to report suspected fraud activity to their immediate manager.

name: Compliance and Financial Crime Team Reporting Obligation
description: The mandatory requirement to report suspected fraud to the specialized Compliance and Financial Crime teams.

name: Adherence to Fraud Policy Procedures
description: The obligation for staff to follow the specific procedures outlined in the bank's fraud policy during the escalation process.

name: Prevent Fraud Training
description: A training section focused on fraud prevention measures for staff, covering procedural adherence and internal security hygiene.

name: Adherence to KYC/AML Procedures
description: A requirement for staff to follow established Know Your Customer and Anti-Money Laundering procedures to prevent fraud.

name: Secure Password Usage
description: An obligation for staff to utilize secure passwords as a fraud prevention measure.

name: Computer Locking Requirement
description: A security requirement for staff to lock their computers to prevent unauthorized access and fraud.

name: Credential Confidentiality
description: A strict prohibition against sharing login credentials with others to maintain system security.

name: Account Monitoring Duty
description: A requirement for staff to monitor their own accounts for suspicious activity.

name: Help Customers Prevent Fraud
description: A training unit focused on empowering staff to educate customers on fraud prevention techniques. It covers security hygiene, monitoring, and specific scam awareness.

name: Educate Customers on Security Hygiene
description: Staff must be able to provide guidance to customers on maintaining strong passwords and implementing two-factor authentication (2FA).

name: Encourage Customer Transaction Monitoring
description: Staff must be able to advise customers on the importance of regularly reviewing their account transactions to spot unauthorized activity.

name: Advise Customers on Phishing Scams
description: Staff must be able to provide advice and warnings to customers regarding the nature and identification of phishing scams.

name: Promote Card Security Practices
description: Staff must be able to promote best practices for the secure use and management of payment cards to customers.

name: Bank Customer
description: The recipient of fraud prevention education and security advice provided by bank staff.

name: Customer Transactions
description: Financial events that customers are encouraged to monitor as a means of fraud prevention.

name: Payment Card
description: The banking instrument subject to security practices promoted to customers to prevent fraud.

name: Direct Debit Guarantee
description: A customer protection product providing refunds for unauthorized, incorrect, or duplicate Direct Debit payments.
context: What It Covers: Unauthorized Direct Debits: Full refund within 10 days

name: Direct Debit Refund Obligation
description: The bank's obligation to provide a full refund within 10 days for unauthorized Direct Debits, wrong amounts charged, or duplicate payments.
context: Unauthorized Direct Debits: Full refund within 10 days
Wrong amount charged: Refund within 10 days

name: Direct Debit Customer
description: Customers utilizing Direct Debit services who are entitled to protection under the Direct Debit Guarantee.

name: Chargeback (Card Fraud) Training
description: A training section covering the chargeback process for card fraud, including the types of disputes handled and the operational timeline for resolution.
context: What It Covers: Unauthorized card transactions: Dispute with card scheme; Merchant error: Dispute with card scheme; Item not received: Dispute with merchant/scheme

name: Understanding Chargeback Dispute Categories
description: Staff must be able to identify the specific scenarios that qualify for a chargeback, including unauthorized transactions, merchant errors, and non-receipt of items.
context: Unauthorized card transactions: Dispute with card scheme
Merchant error: Dispute with card scheme
Item not received: Dispute with merchant/scheme

name: Fraud Reporting Timeline Obligation
description: A requirement that fraud must be reported within a specific window of 120 days to be eligible for the chargeback process.

name: Payment Card
description: The banking product subject to fraud disputes and the chargeback process via card schemes.

name: Unauthorized Card Transaction
description: A financial event where a card transaction is not authorized by the customer, triggering a dispute with the card scheme.
context: Unauthorized card transactions: Dispute with card scheme

name: Customer Reporting Obligation for Unauthorized Transactions
description: The requirement for customers to report unauthorized transactions within a specific timeframe to ensure the bank remains liable for the loss.
context: Unauthorized transactions you report within 120 days
Fraud you failed to report for >120 days

name: Customer Security Measure Obligation
description: The obligation for customers to maintain reasonable security measures to avoid being classified as grossly negligent.
context: If you followed reasonable security measures

name: Gross Negligence via Credential Sharing (Security Warning)
description: Specific customer behaviors, such as sharing passwords or writing down PINs, that constitute gross negligence and void bank liability.

name: Unauthorized Transaction
description: Financial events that were not authorized by the customer and are subject to liability claims if reported within 120 days.
context: Unauthorized transactions you report within 120 days

name: Customer Account Balance
description: The account balance which serves as the upper limit for FirstUK Bank's liability regarding unauthorized transactions.

name: Obligation to Report All Suspicious Activity to Compliance
description: A mandatory requirement for staff to report every concern regarding suspicious activity to the Compliance department, regardless of how obvious the fraud may seem.
context: Correct: Report ALL concerns to Compliance

name: Obligation to Treat All Customer Fraud Reports Seriously
description: Staff are required to acknowledge and take all reports of fraud raised by customers seriously, avoiding the mistake of ignoring these concerns.
context: Correct: Take all fraud reports seriously

name: Prohibition on Sharing Access Credentials
description: A strict rule prohibiting the sharing of access credentials, requiring staff to keep such information private at all times.

name: Convincing Fraudster Persona (Fraud Indicator)
description: A warning that fraudsters are not always obvious and can be highly convincing, requiring staff to maintain a high level of alertness.
context: Correct: Fraudsters can be very convincing; stay alert

name: Module 5 — Reporting Obligations
description: A training unit focused on the various types of reports staff must file, specifically detailing the triggers and processes for Suspicious Activity Reports (SARs).

name: Understanding SAR Filing Requirements
description: Staff must be able to identify when a Suspicious Activity Report is required and follow the correct procedural steps for filing.

name: Suspicious Transaction Exceeding £5,000
description: A specific financial threshold trigger where any transaction over £5,000 deemed suspicious requires reporting.

name: Pattern of Unusual Activity
description: A behavioral indicator where a series of transactions or actions deviate from the customer's normal profile.

name: Potential Money Laundering
description: General indicators that suggest funds may be derived from criminal activity.

name: Fraud Indicators
description: Signals that a transaction or account activity may be fraudulent.

name: Sanctions List Match
description: A match found during screening against official sanctions lists.

name: Rapid Movement of Large Cash Deposits to Unknown Parties
description: A specific scenario where a customer deposits a large sum of cash and immediately withdraws it to an unknown third party.
context: Customer deposits £30k cash, withdraws £30k to unknown party next day

name: SAR Filing Obligation
description: The mandatory requirement to document, report internally, and submit a Suspicious Activity Report to the FCA.

name: SAR Submission Deadline
description: The regulatory requirement to ensure the SAR is submitted to the FCA within a 30-day window.

name: Suspicious Activity Report (SAR)
description: The formal reporting mechanism used to notify the FCA of suspicious financial activity.

name: Currency Transaction Report (CTR) Filing Obligation
description: A mandatory requirement to report cash transactions exceeding £10,000 to the FCA within a specific timeframe. The report must include specific customer and transaction details.

name: Cash Transaction Exceeding £10,000 (CTR Trigger)
description: A specific financial threshold trigger where a cash transaction over £10,000 necessitates the filing of a Currency Transaction Report.
context: Customer withdraws £15,000 in cash → File CTR

name: Customer
description: The individual associated with the cash transaction who must be identified in the CTR filing as either new or existing.
context: Whether customer is new or existing

name: Cash Transaction
description: A financial event involving cash that, when exceeding £10,000, triggers a regulatory reporting requirement.

name: Counterparty Transaction Report (CCTR) Filing Obligation
description: A mandatory reporting requirement for specific types of transactions, including those involving high-risk jurisdictions, politically exposed persons, or international wire transfers.
context: When to File: Transaction involving high-risk countries
Transaction with PEP or sanctioned party

name: High-Risk Country Transaction
description: A financial transaction involving a high-risk country that triggers the requirement to file a Counterparty Transaction Report.

name: PEP or Sanctioned Party Transaction
description: A transaction involving a Politically Exposed Person (PEP) or a sanctioned party that necessitates a CCTR filing.
context: Transaction with PEP or sanctioned party

name: International Wire Transfer
description: A wire transfer sent outside of the UK which serves as a trigger for a Counterparty Transaction Report.

name: CCTR Customer Details
description: The customer information that must be included as part of a Counterparty Transaction Report.

name: CCTR Risk Assessment
description: The risk assessment component that must be documented and reported within the Counterparty Transaction Report.

name: Internal Whistleblowing Reporting Obligation
description: The requirement for staff to report suspected fraud, policy violations, compliance breaches, or misconduct internally by speaking to a manager or HR.
context: How to Report: Internal: Speak to manager or HR

name: Confidential Whistleblowing Reporting Obligation
description: The option and obligation to report concerns confidentially via the Data Protection Officer.
context: Confidential: Speak to Data Protection Officer (dpo@firstuk.bank)

name: External Whistleblowing Reporting Obligation
description: The process for reporting concerns to the external regulatory body, the FCA.

name: Non-Retaliation Prohibition
description: A strict prohibition against retaliating against staff members who act as whistleblowers.

name: Whistleblower Confidentiality Obligation
description: The requirement to maintain the confidentiality of the whistleblower during and after the reporting process.

name: Colleague Fraud (Whistleblowing Warning Sign)
description: Suspicion of fraudulent activity carried out by a colleague within the bank.

name: Policy Violation (Whistleblowing Warning Sign)
description: Observation of actions that violate established bank policies.

name: Compliance Breach (Whistleblowing Warning Sign)
description: Observation of failures to adhere to regulatory or legal compliance requirements.

name: General Misconduct (Whistleblowing Warning Sign)
description: Witnessing general professional misconduct within the organization.

name: Detailed Activity Documentation Requirement
description: Staff are required to maintain comprehensive records of suspicious activities, including the timing, participants, specific details of the activity, the rationale for suspicion, and the resulting actions and outcomes.

name: Customer File Retention Obligation
description: A mandatory requirement to retain customer files for a period of 6 years following the closure of the account.

name: Transaction Record Retention Obligation
description: A mandatory requirement to retain all transaction records for a period of 6 years.

name: KYC/AML Record Retention Obligation
description: A mandatory requirement to retain Know Your Customer (KYC) and Anti-Money Laundering (AML) documentation for a period of 5 to 6 years.

name: SAR Record Retention Obligation
description: A mandatory requirement to retain Suspicious Activity Reports (SARs) for a minimum period of 5 years.

name: Secure Record Storage and Access Obligation
description: Requirements for the physical and digital security of records, including the use of locked cabinets, encryption for digital files, restricted access for authorized staff, and regular backups.

name: Module 6 — Consequences of Non-Compliance
description: A training module detailing the various penalties and repercussions FirstUK Bank faces due to regulatory failures. It covers financial fines, regulatory actions, and reputational damage.
context: What Happens If You Don't Comply?

name: AML Compliance Obligation
description: The requirement to adhere to Anti-Money Laundering (AML) regulations to avoid significant financial penalties and regulatory enforcement.
context: AML violations: Up to £10M+ per incident

name: GDPR Compliance Obligation
description: The obligation to comply with General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) to prevent heavy fines based on revenue or fixed amounts.
context: GDPR breaches: Up to €20M or 4% revenue

name: Customer Protection Obligation
description: The duty to ensure customer protection standards are met to avoid substantial fines from the FCA.

name: Consequences of Non-Compliance Training
description: A training section detailing the severe legal, professional, and financial repercussions for staff members who fail to adhere to banking regulations and internal policies.

name: Prohibition of Tipping-Off
description: A strict legal requirement that staff must not warn a customer that they are being screened for money laundering or other criminal activities.
context: Tipping-off (warning customer of screening): Criminal offense

name: Prevention of Money Laundering Facilitation
description: The obligation for staff to avoid any actions that facilitate money laundering, the breach of which carries significant criminal penalties.
context: Money laundering facilitation: Up to 14 years prison

name: Fraud Prevention Obligation
description: The requirement for staff to act with integrity to prevent fraud, with failure resulting in potential imprisonment.

name: Data Protection Compliance
description: The obligation to handle customer data according to protection laws to avoid criminal liability and prison sentences.
context: Data protection breach: Up to 2 years prison

name: Consequence Management Case Studies
description: A training section focusing on real-world examples of banking and corporate failures to illustrate the consequences of compliance breaches. It covers AML failures, account fraud, and GDPR violations.

name: Ignoring Suspicious Transactions (AML Red Flag)
description: A behavioral warning sign where staff fail to act upon or ignore transactions that exhibit suspicious characteristics, leading to massive regulatory failure.

name: Unauthorized Account Creation (Fraud Indicator)
description: The act of creating customer accounts without proper authorization, often driven by internal pressure to meet performance targets.
context: Staff created fake accounts without authorization
Pressure to meet targets; ignored ethics

name: Data Sharing Without Consent (GDPR Violation)
description: The unauthorized sharing of user data without obtaining the necessary legal consent, violating data protection rights.

name: Ethical Conduct and Target Adherence
description: The obligation for staff to maintain ethical standards and avoid fraudulent activity even when under pressure to meet business targets.
context: Pressure to meet targets; ignored ethics

name: User Data Consent Requirement
description: The mandatory requirement to respect user data rights and obtain explicit consent before sharing personal data.

name: Suspicious Money Flow
description: High-volume suspicious financial movements, exemplified by the £200B flow in the Danske Bank case.

name: Fake Accounts
description: Accounts created fraudulently by staff without customer authorization.
context: Staff created fake accounts without authorization

name: Mandatory Training Completion
description: Staff are required to complete all assigned training modules and their associated assessments to ensure competency.
context: Complete Training: Finish all modules and assessments

name: Escalation of Uncertainties
description: Staff must escalate any queries or uncertainties to their manager or the compliance department.
context: Ask Questions: If unsure, escalate to manager/compliance

name: Adherence to SOPs and Policies
description: Staff must follow established Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) and bank policies, specifically those regarding AML, customer identification, and privacy.
context: Follow Procedures: Use the SOPs and policies [[policy_aml]], [[policy_customer_identification]], [[policy_privacy]], etc.

name: Reporting of Suspicious Activity
description: Staff are obligated to report any suspicious activity and are explicitly instructed not to ignore such indicators.
context: Report Issues: Don't ignore suspicious activity

name: Documentation of Actions
description: Staff must maintain detailed records of the actions they have taken in response to bank procedures or incidents.
context: Document Actions: Keep records of what you did

name: Annual Refresher Training Attendance
description: Staff must attend refresher training on an annual basis to stay updated on banking regulations and procedures.
context: Stay Updated: Attend refresher training annually

name: Maintenance of Professional Ethics
description: Staff are required to maintain high standards of integrity and ethics in their professional conduct.

name: Assessment Quiz
description: A final assessment module requiring a minimum score of 80% to pass. It tests staff knowledge across AML, KYC, GDPR, Fraud, and reporting obligations.

name: AML Screening Requirements Knowledge
description: Staff must demonstrate an understanding of the requirements surrounding AML screening as part of the assessment quiz.

name: KYC Document Validity Knowledge
description: Staff must be able to determine the validity of KYC documents as part of the assessment quiz.

name: GDPR Customer Rights Knowledge
description: Staff must understand the specific rights granted to customers under GDPR regulations.

name: Fraud Red Flag Recognition
description: Staff must be able to identify and recognize red flags associated with fraudulent activity.

name: Reporting Obligations Knowledge
description: Staff must understand their specific duties and obligations regarding the reporting of suspicious activity or compliance breaches.

name: Consequences of Violations Knowledge
description: Staff must be aware of the penalties and consequences resulting from compliance violations.

name: Escalation Duty for Missing Proof of Address
description: Staff are prohibited from opening an account if the customer cannot provide proof of address and must instead escalate the matter to a manager.
context: What should you do if a customer can't provide proof of address? A: Don't open account, escalate to manager

name: Anti-Tipping-Off Prohibition
description: Staff are strictly prohibited from informing a customer that they have matched a sanctions screen, as tipping-off is illegal.
context: Can you tell a customer they matched a sanctions screen? A: No, tipping-off is illegal

name: Customer Data Retention Requirement
description: Customer data must be retained for a period of 6 years following the closure of the account.
context: How long must you keep customer data? A: 6 years after account closure

name: Direct Debit Guarantee Refund Obligation
description: Under the Direct Debit Guarantee, a full refund must be provided for unauthorized Direct Debits within 10 days.
context: What's the Direct Debit Guarantee? A: Full refund of unauthorized DD within 10 days

name: Comprehensive Staff Training Program
description: The overall training program consisting of 6 modules covering regulatory compliance, fraud detection, and data protection. Completion requires a minimum assessment score of 80% and a signed acknowledgment.

name: Understanding AML and Sanctions Requirements
description: Staff must demonstrate a comprehensive understanding of the bank's Anti-Money Laundering (AML) and sanctions compliance requirements.

name: Knowledge of KYC Document Requirements
description: Staff must be able to identify and verify the specific documentation required for Know Your Customer (KYC) processes.

name: Understanding GDPR and Data Rights
description: Staff must understand the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) and the specific data rights afforded to customers.

name: Identification of Fraud Red Flags
description: Staff must be capable of recognizing and identifying specific indicators and red flags associated with fraudulent activity.

name: Knowledge of Reporting Obligations
description: Staff must know the specific mandatory reporting duties required when suspicious activity or compliance breaches are identified.

name: Understanding of Consequences
description: Staff must understand the potential consequences resulting from non-compliance with bank policies and regulatory requirements.

name: Mandatory Training Completion and Assessment
description: Staff are obligated to complete all six training modules and achieve a score of 80% or higher on the assessment quiz.

name: Signed Training Acknowledgment
description: Staff must formally sign an acknowledgment to confirm the completion of the training program.

name: Compliance Training Completion Obligation
description: A mandatory requirement for staff to complete the designated compliance training and formally acknowledge their completion via signature.

name: Policy Adherence Obligation
description: The requirement for staff to understand and strictly follow all of FirstUK Bank's established policies and procedures.
context: Will follow all procedures going forward

name: Concern Reporting Obligation
description: The requirement for staff to be knowledgeable about the correct channels and methods for reporting compliance or policy concerns.

name: Violation Consequences Awareness Obligation
description: The requirement for staff to acknowledge and understand the disciplinary or legal consequences resulting from policy violations.

name: Annual Renewal Training
description: A mandatory annual refresher training program for staff that must be completed by January 15, 2027.

name: Annual Training Completion Obligation
description: Staff are required to complete their refresher training by the deadline of January 15, 2027, and must schedule this training via email by December 31, 2026.
context: Schedule training: Email training@firstuk.bank by December 31, 2026
